transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because once I start worrying, I can’t seem to shut it off. Even when I’ve made my list, checked the dates, and done everything I can reasonably do, my mind just keeps going.
Is your worry usually about one particular thing or many different things?

It’s many different things, not just one. My mind will jump from the exhibition schedule, to my daughter’s travel plans, to whether the house gutters need fixing. And then even small things start to feel like they could turn into something much bigger.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to ignore them or make them stop?

Yes, I suppose so. It’s not like a single phrase repeating, but the worries keep coming back even when I try to tell myself I’ve done what I can. I’ll make a list, check the dates, go over things, and then my mind still won’t let it go.
Do you have any thoughts that are intrusive or unwanted, and that you try to suppress or ignore?

Yes, I do have unwanted worries that come in and keep coming back. I try to push them aside and remind myself I’ve made the list, checked the dates, and done what I can, but once the worrying starts, I can’t seem to turn it off.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors to reduce your worries?

I don’t think I have rituals, exactly. I might check a list or look at the calendar again, but it’s more trying to reassure myself than something I feel I have to do in a set way. Nothing like a specific routine I must repeat.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of your worries?

Yes, somewhat. I still do my usual things, like keeping up with the garden and going to book club, but I’ve started stepping back from some things. With the exhibition planning, I’ve been turning down parts of it because it just feels harder to manage than it used to, and I’m less prepared when I do show up.
Do you experience significant fear or anxiety in response to your worries?

Yes. It’s not usually panic, but I do get anxious. My mind jumps from the exhibition schedule to my daughter’s travel plans to things around the house, like whether the gutters need fixing. Then small things start to feel like they could turn into much bigger problems.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?
I don’t think so, not really. I get worried and tense, but I haven’t noticed feeling especially sad or depressed lately.
Has something very stressful or traumatic happened to you recently or in the past?
Yes… my friend died about seven months ago. After that, I tried to keep our projects going, and I think that’s when all of this really started. It’s been going on since then.
Did you notice a change in how you handle daily tasks or responsibilities after your friend passed away?

Yes, I did notice some change. I still keep up with things like the garden and my book club, but I’m not as on top of everything as I used to be. I’ll show up less prepared, and with the exhibition planning, I’ve started turning down parts of it because it just feels harder to manage now.
Have you felt emotionally numb or detached from others since your friend passed away?
I’m not sure I’d call it numb. I’ve still felt things, and I don’t think I’ve been especially detached from people. Maybe I’ve been a bit more caught up in my own thoughts, but not cut off, no.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the day, nearly every day, since your friend passed away?
I don’t think it’s been like that most of the day, nearly every day. I’ve been sad about it, of course, but I wouldn’t describe myself as feeling empty all the time.
Do you avoid certain tasks or decisions because you fear making a mistake or losing control?

Yes, a bit. I still do things like the garden and book club, but I’m not as prepared as I used to be. And with the exhibition planning, I’ve been turning down parts of it because it feels harder to manage, and I worry I won’t handle it properly.
Have you been consistently thinking about your friend who passed away over the past seven months?
I’m not really sure. I do think about her sometimes, of course, but I haven’t been keeping track of how often. It doesn’t feel like I can say it’s been consistent every day or anything like that.
Have you been having intense feelings of sadness or longing for your friend who passed away over the past seven months?
I don’t know that I’d call it intense. I do miss her, and I get sad when I think about her, but I haven’t really noticed it as this strong longing all the time over the whole seven months.
Have you had difficulty accepting the loss of your friend?
I’m not sure. I know she’s gone, and I understand that, but I haven’t really thought about whether I’ve had trouble accepting it. It’s sad, but I can’t say much more than that.
Have you been having trouble moving on or finding a sense of closure since your friend passed away?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve felt stuck exactly. I miss her, but I haven’t thought of it in terms of closure or moving on. It’s more just… I know she’s gone, and sometimes it feels sad.
Have you been having trouble accepting that your life will never be the same without your friend?

I don’t think I’ve really felt that way. I know things are different without her, and that’s sad, but I haven’t been focused on my whole life never being the same. It’s more just occasional sadness when I think about her.
Do you think your worrying and anxiety are mainly about your friend who passed away or about a wide range of everyday things?

It’s more about a range of everyday things, I think. My mind jumps from the exhibition schedule to my daughter’s travel plans, then to whether the gutters on the house need fixing. Little things start to feel like they could turn into much bigger problems.
Do you think your worrying and anxiety started right after your friend passed away or did they develop over time after the loss?
It started pretty soon after she died, I think. At first I was trying to keep our projects moving, and then the worrying just sort of kept going. It’s been about seven months now.
